title: Comparative Study on I Gel Insertion Conditions using DexmedetomidinePropofol versus Fentanyl Propofol
author: Kakileti Vani Subrahmaneyswari
license_note: Zenodo record metadata license field: cc-by-4.0

steps.title: Select eligible participants
steps.instruction: Recruit male and female patients aged 18–60 years scheduled for short surgical procedures under general anaesthesia, classified as ASA I or II and Mallampati (MPG) I or II, after obtaining informed consent and completing pre‑anaesthetic evaluation.

steps.title: Randomize into study groups
steps.instruction: Randomly assign each enrolled participant, in a double‑blinded manner, to either Group D (dexmedetomidine) or Group F (fentanyl) using a pre‑generated randomisation schedule.

steps.title: Prepare study medication
steps.instruction: For Group D, calculate dexmedetomidine dose at 1 µg per kg body weight; for Group F, calculate fentanyl dose at 1 µg per kg body weight. Draw the calculated volume into a syringe labeled only with a study code to maintain blinding.

steps.title: Administer study drug
steps.instruction: Administer the prepared dexmedetomidine or fentanyl intravenously over a standard period (as per institutional practice) before induction.

steps.title: Induce anesthesia
steps.instruction: Induce general anaesthesia with propofol (dose per institutional protocol) following the study drug infusion.

steps.title: Insert i‑gel airway
steps.instruction: After confirming loss of consciousness, insert the i‑gel® supraglottic airway device according to the manufacturer’s guidelines.

steps.title: Assess insertion conditions
steps.instruction: Evaluate ease of i‑gel insertion, jaw‑relaxation grade, patient movement, coughing, gagging, and overall conditions using the predefined scoring system.

steps.title: Monitor hemodynamic parameters
steps.instruction: Record heart rate, systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, and mean arterial pressure at baseline (pre‑drug), after study drug infusion, after propofol induction, and at 1, 3, 5, and 10 minutes after i‑gel insertion.

steps.title: Remove i‑gel post‑surgery
steps.instruction: At the conclusion of the surgical procedure, remove the i‑gel device and document any complications.
